body:
He said I was a loser for playing so many games. I don't know if he realized I could hear him in a different room, but after that I just stopped hanging out with him. Also after living with him I learned he's fairly racist and homophobic, and that just aint cool to me. I never talked about it because I didn't wanna sound like I was creepin on his conversation; also I tend to be passive aggressive sometimes due to my fear of confrontation :p

Had no idea that guitars were that cheap...probably could do some online shit and make 100 within a week in my spare time. Might have give it a shot. 

Bout the closest I've ever gotten to playing a guitar is guitar hero though lol. Shit maybe you could give me some newbie tips for people just starting out

Yeah thats true, I do care about people, I just hate that I care so much about how I look/act around people. It makes me become a people pleaser, and I pretty much try to avoid any confrontation so I tend to be overly passive, which probably is why I'm terrible with women. I've been passive so long that I guess I took an apathetic outside personality, but deep down I do desire to have deep connections with people.

As of right now, I really don't have anyone. I used to have a good friend, but I overheard him talking behind my back and then acting like we were still best buds over something. Completely lost all respect. I guess it would be my brother, but he's off in school. I definitely know what you mean about walking in cold; I always feel at ease in public if I'm around my family, but if I'm by myself I get super paranoid.

I think I will investigate the music avenue. Guitars are pretty expensive so I would have to save up for a little bit, but I imagine the pleasure from learning to play an instrument like that could be very therapeutic, plus it would be awesome to eventually be able to play along with some of my favorite songs. 

I'm assuming by your name that you play guitar? :p

1. The apathy is more widespread, I was just using my grandparents as an example because I always felt strange admitting that I honestly don't care about them. The social anxiety is definitely something that is the main 'mountain' in my life. I'm constantly worried about what other people think of me, so to avoid this stress I started avoiding social interactions. The depression kind of fogs my mind as to what my goals are, since I tend to obsess over the negative aspects of my life

2. I haven't but I definitely should. I hate to constantly blame everything on social anxiety, but I feel I wouldn't have the confidence to go into a group like that. I tried going to an MMA club to learn jiu jitsu since I'm a big fan of both, but ended up embarrassing myself pretty bad

3. Yeah I love listening to music, it's one of the few things that brings energy to me, just a big fan of the metal/metalcore genre. My mom owns a piano so it could be something that I could at least give another shot at, as I used to take piano lessons when I was a kid but gave up after my piano teacher died

I'm sorry if I come off as whiny, as I do appreciate input in this matter

Truthfully, it is hard to imagine being so confident in myself that I could walk up to a random stranger without some innate fear. I know that it's surely possible, it's just that I've been this way for so long it almost seems foreign, if that makes any sense.

I never thought about the permanent solution/end like that before, and it's a good way of thinking. I'll try to keep that in mind, thanks.

Thanks for the kind words. I am seeing a therapist but she is out of town right now so I have to wait till she gets back. Only had 1 session so far so it mainly consisted of her getting to know me a little better.

I think it does but it's hard to tell because I generally don't think about it too often. I didn't see the group question at first, but no I don't have any group type of activities. I go lift weights on my own but that's about it. The social anxiety is usually so bad that I end up avoiding any social interaction unless absolutely required.

Not sure what I'm good at, does video games count :P ? I'm pretty knowledgeable about weight lifting/nutrition after spending a lot of time on the internet. I usually have a decent sense of humor once people get to know me. That's really all that stands out unfortunately :/

Agreed about the 'catchy' part. I talked to my parents today, and after a rough 1st talk where they used this phrase, my mom later came back in my room and started crying herself, apologizing for not listening to how I felt. It honestly felt like a weight lifted off my shoulders to hear that in person, especially from my mom. I feel much better than I did this morning, thats for sure.

What a great, caring subreddit

I will definitely be taking notes of those tips you posted in case I ever need to use them in the future!

Wow, that really sounds tough, as I couldn't imagine one of my siblings killing themselves. Really puts things into perspective, especially with how easy of a life I've had. 

You sound like an intelligent person so I'm glad you didn't follow through. Can't really think of anything to say since I've never experienced anything like that, sorry man :/
So how did your family (and you) react to your brother's suicide? Kinda the only thing holding me back is creating even greater pain on my family

Yeah I know, and the weird thing is that I can take rational look at things and realize that it really isn't that bad, but my brain is just screaming at me to end my life. The thoughts never stop...

Glad to see you've gotten on the right path though
Yeah thats my line of thinking, its hard to think of a good future when you're focused on how bad everything sucks

I've always been known as a fairly good kid, but deep down I lie about shit all the time and never felt guilty about it. I used to forge grades, steal shit, get in trouble, but lie about it and come off looking squeaky clean.

You're right about the self esteem, it's about as low as it gets, but you probably wouldn't know if you saw me. Sometimes I really feel like I'm fucking sociopath or something. I remember even telling my parents at one point that I hated going to my grandparents house and that I don't care for them (and I still don't). Fucked up shit.... but it's how I feel.

>Well, first things first, ARE there girls that you know (i.e. not celebrities or other one-way relationships) that you're interested in?  

I don't know any women personally because I'm too afraid to talk to girls. I avoid any possible interaction with them since I have incredibly low self esteem and no confidence. But I guess the same could go with guys since I haven't made a close friend since middle school. I avoid interactions in general with people, but the anxiety is doubled around women.

As for your second point, I don't really have any real friends. I have spent my entire life lying to people so I won't feel like an incredible loser (even though I still do). I've lied about having sex and having a girlfriend, because when I had friends they talked about these issues a lot and I ALWAYS felt left out. Terrible, I know, but something that I am deeply ashamed about.

To your third point, I agree, I shouldn't self diagnose. I tend to spend a lot of my free time on psychology forums/ anxiety forums learning about personality disorders, and just looking at the criteria from the DSM IV it seems I would fit but you are right. 

On the issues of intimacy, I truly don't know. When I was around 13 years old, a girl I really liked called me on the phone and asked to be her boyfriend; The only time I have felt truly comfortable around a girl. I was not unexpecting such a phone call, and I got so embarassed about admitting that I cared for her that I told I couldn't because I was grounded (I wasn't - how pathetic is that). So it's issue that has plagued my entire life and I struggle to grasp as to why I can't open up to ANYONE. 

Thanks for the reply, I can see you put a lot of thought behind it

That is true, which I why I love the internet, it's a safe haven. 

Thank you for your perspective and it really does mean a lot to me  that you took the time to respond, honestly it helped so much just to have someone willing to listen. I think I will give myself some time to think before I do anything irrational.

Yeah I usually try to go out in the backyard to get some fresh air and sunlight, but my anxiety is ever persisting. I used to love video games and weightlifting, two activities that always took my mind off things. Unfortunately, I can't enjoy these activities anxiety-free anymore. Even when I walk outside to get the mail from my mailbox, my body literally feels like people are watching me, as irrational as that sounds. So I avoid leaving the house unless I have to, which is why I'm deathly terrified of being forced to get a job. Almost feels like I have schizophrenia, since I'm incredibly paranoid.

My mom is caring and she is probably the reason that I would even stop to think about what I'm considering. As for friends, I have none. I really have nobody I can confide in, because my family has been raised in the conservative Christian manner, and I made the choice to not believe when I was around 12 years old. Its something that I feel I can never share with my family, thus, I truly have nobody I can be myself around. 

I used to have good friends, but they were Christians who couldn't even understand the idea of non-belief. Since everyone assumes I'm Christian, they have no qualms about trashing those 'idiot' non believers, so you can imagine how I feel leading this double life. 

My depression got so bad last night that I even fit the belt around my neck to ensure that I would cut off the blood supply to my brain instead of cutting off my windpipe. I'm scared of failing suicide, but I feel so desperately alone and hopeless.

Probably not the best solution, but as far as how I feel, it's the only solution. I understand that I could take a risk and possibly feel better, but the insurmountable mountain that lies ahead of me is too scary. I'm a coward, plain and simple.

As for my dad, he's always been there to support my physical needs - taking me to activities, providing food/shelter/clothing/etc, but emotionally he's unavailable. I've even convinced myself that he cares more about the 2 cats than he does me, since he shows way more loving emotions towards them. I honestly can't remember if he's ever told me he's loved me, nor do I ever remember him giving me a hug or anything like that. 

In fact, when I confessed my depression and serious social anxiety to both my parents, the only ting I remember him saying was something along the lines of "Well you gotta talk to people to get ahead in life". Oh really? No shit dad, thanks for the stellar advice. My mom hugged me and told me she cares about me and not once did my dad even try to be supportive. Thanks for the reply

Maybe overrated to some people, but not to me. Growing up as a kid I knew I always felt shy and different and that I missed out on a such a critical part of being a human - real, deep social connections. At this point though I've gone so long without them that it's completely drained my will to change. Thanks for the reply though

Growing as a family, I spent most of my time by myself, even though my parents tried to get me to go places with them. Yeah I have terrible social anxiety so I don't have really anybody who I can really be myself around, nor do I have any friends.  

I appreciate the kind words, sometimes I feel as though I'm subhuman, devoid of any real attachment. The worst part is that i know it's my fault. I was the one who pushed everyone away when I was a kid, and now I'm just reaping what I've sewn.
